slides.0.title: Level 2 final assessment
slides.0.subtitle: Raw material, distillation, maturation, rules: the four questions for any spirit
slides.1.title: Level 2 key points
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Principles
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Pot stills keep flavour, column stills are purer; keep the hearts; oak brings extraction, subtraction, oxidation and evaporation; age statements give the youngest component; tropical maturation is faster
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Whisky
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Scotch 3 years, 40%, five regions, Islay peat; Irish 3 years, single pot still; Bourbon 51% corn, new charred barrels; Tennessee maple-charcoal filtering; the 2021 Japanese standard
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Other spirits
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Rhum agricole from cane juice (Martinique AOC 1996); tequila from Blue Weber, mixto at least 51%, Reposado/Añejo/Extra Añejo; mezcal pit-roasted; London Dry is a method; liqueurs generally at least 100 g/L sugar
slides.1.content: CMS orals often ask for a spirit’s raw material and key rules: answer raw material first, then distillation and maturation.
slides.2.componentProps.slide.title: 📋 Level 2 final assessment
What style is most typical of column distillation?
Vodka and grain whisky mostly use column stills.
Which of these is not a protected Scotch region?
The five: Highland, Lowland, Speyside, Campbeltown, Islay.
How long must Straight Bourbon mature at minimum?
Single pot still is a distinctive style of which country?
A mix of malted and unmalted barley.
What minimum share of agave sugar must tequila mixto have?
What is the ageing period for Tequila Reposado?
A. 2 months to under a year
What may be added to London Dry Gin after distillation?
B. Water and minimal sugar (≤0.1 g/L)
Flavour may come only from redistilled natural botanicals.
What is the minimum sugar for a “crème de” liqueur?
Crème de cassis needs at least 400 g.
